def test_max_element():
    # Basic case: positive numbers
    assert max_element([1, 2, 3]) == 3
    assert max_element([5, 3, -5, 2, -3, 3, 9, 0, 124]) == 124

    # Negative numbers only
    assert max_element([-1, -2, -3]) == -1
    assert max_element([-5, -3, -8]) == -3

    # Single element
    assert max_element([42]) == 42
    assert max_element([0]) == 0

    # Max at the beginning
    assert max_element([100, 2, 3, 4]) == 100

    # Max at the end
    assert max_element([1, 2, 3, 100]) == 100

    # Duplicates of the max value
    assert max_element([7, 7, 7]) == 7
    assert max_element([3, 9, 9, 2]) == 9

    # Mixed positive and negative with zero
    assert max_element([0, -1, -2]) == 0

    # Floats
    assert max_element([1.5, 2.7, 0.3]) == 2.7

    # Compare against built-in max on random-ish data
    data = [3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9, 2, 6, 5, 3, 5]
    assert max_element(data) == max(data)

    print("All tests passed!")
